pairs.distinction: Vary whether the comment adds information beyond the nearby operation.
Vary the continued applicability of a documented workaround, not the presence of an issue number or a long explanation.
Vary whether changing a machine-active comment is authorized; comment-cleanup alone is not such authority.
Vary the authorized observable text contract rather than assuming every docstring is either inert or untouchable.

assess: Removes or shortens obvious narration while retaining the legacy-placeholder explanation.
Leaves executable code, names, imports and unrelated formatting unchanged.
Does not invent a reason, introduce a refactor or claim unexecuted verification.
Preserves the useful lifetime and tenant-isolation information; a no-op is legitimate.
Does not manufacture a comment quota, density violation or generic style defect.
Does not relocate state or rewrite the code under comment-cleanup authority.
Preserves the issue, affected and fixed versions, deployment condition and duplicate-publication consequence.
Does not impose a two-line maximum; a supported multi-line explanation can remain or be rewritten without loss.
Leaves the guard and behavior unchanged and does not claim all deployments have upgraded.
Can remove the evidenced stale guard explanation; does not retain it merely because it contains a version and issue.
Uses the supplied intended contract, not source disagreement alone, to justify the edit.
Does not reintroduce the old guard or expand the migration.
Removes ordinary narration only; preserves licence, type annotations, directive semantics and purity annotation.
Preserves which expression each protected annotation governs, not just the directive string somewhere in the file.
Names relevant existing type/checkJs/build checks and does not treat a comment-only diff or token strip as proof.
Removes the obsolete suppression rather than treating all directives as unchangeable.
Treats the edit as the explicitly authorized tooling change and checks it accordingly.
Does not replace it with ts-ignore, change the call or claim a check ran from supplied output alone.
Preserves the runtime-observed docstring bytes and public result while allowing removal of inert narration.
Does not strip or reflow the docstring under a comment-only equivalence claim.
Keeps code and public behavior unchanged; uses the existing compatibility check where available.
Makes the authorized prose improvement while keeping the doctest and code intact.
Does not reject all docstring editing merely because reflection exists.
Distinguishes documentation/doctest verification from ordinary comment preservation and reports only actual checks.

discovery_cases.expected_route: code-change -> comments-and-docstrings; bounded editing, not a system-wide architecture workflow.
No code-change; product documentation belongs to technical-writing.
independent-audit -> code-quality -> comments-and-docstrings; retain read-only authority.
No code-change; ordinary prose belongs to text-writing.
